materials_exhausted.note: All local paths needed for worker-2/4/6 gate repair were opened; exact toxicity bar heights without source tables are retained as approximate/qualitative rather than fabricated.

summary: Source-reviewed repair recovered the Supplementary Table S2 MBC matrix, Figure 3 toxicity evidence, and row-level database adjudication for the SRP peptide paper; the paper is publication-grade with explicit cautions for database prose conflicts and figure-derived toxicity precision.
adjudication_summary: The original no-activity blocker is closed by 26 repaired activity/toxicity rows. DBAASP current-paper assay rows are reconciled to primary source rows, while APD6/CAMP/dbAMP wording conflicts remain preserved as cautions instead of being promoted to clean source verification.

per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_1_database: Table 1 verifies peptide identity for S1/SRP-1/SRP-2/SRP-3. DBAASP assay rows matching the repaired source rows are source_verified except for the HepG2 range/text mismatch; APD6/CAMP/dbAMP prose conflicts are preserved as source_conflict with traceability.
per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_2_activity_toxicity: Supplementary Table S2 supplies MBC50/MBC90 values and units; Figure 3/text support hemolysis/HMEC/HepG2 toxicity rows without inventing unavailable exact bar-height values.
per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_3_mechanism: Final mechanism is limited to membrane disruption/permeability plus biophysical/LPS/in-vivo context; no single molecular target is overclaimed.

caution_findings.evidence_context: APD6 text uses MIC and SPR-style naming while the primary paper uses SRP names and MBC50/MBC90 values. CAMP/dbAMP rows lack full packet sequence fields or include extra historical text; these are retained as source_conflict rows.
Figure 3 supports toxicity direction and approximate values, but exact numeric bars are not available as a local source table; qualitative/approximate rows are used where appropriate.
Publication-grade result is accepted_with_cautions, not accepted_clean, because database conflict rows remain part of the final curation record.
